description: Standalone Kubernetes resource management desktop application with tree navigation and resource views.

tech_stack.notes: Use electron-vite for Electron + Vite integration. Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/vite plugin. shadcn/ui components copied into src/renderer/components/ui/. Main process handles kubeconfig and k8s API calls via IPC; renderer is the React UI.

architecture.main_process: Reads ~/.kube/config, creates k8s API clients, exposes IPC handlers for resource queries

architecture.ipc_pattern: renderer calls ipcRenderer.invoke('k8s:<resource>:<action>', ...args), main process returns serialized data

stories.title: kind cluster setup script and test fixture manifests
stories.description: Create a local testing environment using kind (Kubernetes IN Docker). (3) A teardown script `scripts/teardown-kind.sh` that deletes the cluster. The setup script must be idempotent: if the cluster already exists, it skips creation. stories.title: Name filter input beside namespace selector

stories.title: Prometheus endpoint configuration and metrics IPC
stories.description: Allow the user to configure a Prometheus base URL (and optional Bearer token) that the app uses to query pod metrics. The configuration is persisted via Electron's electron-store (or a plain JSON config file in userData). Expose IPC handlers in the main process that query Prometheus range queries for CPU, memory, network, and disk metrics for a given pod.
acceptance_criteria: A settings entry stores `prometheusUrl: string` and `prometheusToken: string` (optional); defaults to empty strings
A settings UI (modal or dedicated settings section reachable from the AppBar) lets the user enter and save the Prometheus base URL and optional Bearer token
IPC handler `prometheus:config:get` returns `{ prometheusUrl, prometheusToken }`
IPC handler `prometheus:config:set` accepts `{ prometheusUrl, prometheusToken }` and persists the values

IPC handler `prometheus:pod:metrics` accepts `{ namespace, podName, step?, rangeMinutes? }` and returns `{ cpu: DataPoint[], memory: DataPoint[], networkRx: DataPoint[], networkTx: DataPoint[], diskRead: DataPoint[], diskWrite: DataPoint[] }` where `DataPoint = { timestamp: number, value: number }`
Queries use Prometheus HTTP API `/api/v1/query_range`; default range is last 30 minutes, step 60s
CPU query: `rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>',container!=''}[5m])`
Memory query: `container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>',container!=''}`
Network Rx: `rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
Network Tx: `rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
Disk read: `rate(container_fs_reads_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
Disk write: `rate(container_fs_writes_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
If Prometheus URL is not configured, handler returns an error `{ error: 'Prometheus not configured' }`
If the HTTP request fails, handler returns `{ error: '<message>' }` without crashing the main process
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Use Node's built-in `fetch` (Node 18+) or the `axios` package for HTTP requests in the main process. Store config with `electron-store` package (add to dependencies). Serialize all response data to plain objects before sending over IPC. Sum multi-container series client-side or aggregate with `sum by (pod)` in the PromQL query.

stories.title: Pod metrics graphs in pod detail panel
stories.description: Display CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O metric graphs inside the pod detail panel. When a pod is selected in the resource list, the detail panel shows a 'Metrics' section with four line charts populated via the `prometheus:pod:metrics` IPC handler. Charts auto-refresh every 60 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Pod detail panel includes a 'Metrics' section below the existing pod info
Four charts are rendered: CPU Usage (cores), Memory Usage (bytes formatted as MiB/GiB), Network I/O (Rx and Tx on same chart), Disk I/O (Read and Write on same chart)
Charts use `recharts` (add to dependencies); each is a `LineChart` with a time-based X axis and labeled Y axis
On mount the component calls `window.api.getPrometheusPodMetrics({ namespace, podName })` and populates the charts
A loading spinner is shown while the request is in flight
If Prometheus is not configured, the Metrics section shows a message 'Prometheus not configured — add URL in Settings'
If the request errors, an inline error message is shown with a retry button
Charts refresh automatically every 60 seconds while the pod detail panel is open
Switching to a different pod cancels the pending refresh and starts a fresh fetch for the new pod
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Install `recharts` and `@types/recharts` (if needed). Format bytes on Y axis with a custom tick formatter (`bytes => (bytes / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1) + ' MiB'`). Use `useEffect` with a `setInterval` for auto-refresh; clear interval on unmount. Network chart: two `<Line>` series (Rx = blue, Tx = orange). Disk chart: two `<Line>` series (Read = green, Write = red). Add `window.api.getPrometheusPodMetrics` and `window.api.getPrometheusConfig` / `window.api.setPrometheusConfig` to the preload `contextBridge`.

stories.title: Pod shell exec in bottom drawer tab
stories.description: Allow users to open an interactive shell inside a pod container. When a pod is selected in the resource list, a 'Shell' button appears in the pod detail panel. Clicking it opens a resizable bottom drawer containing a terminal tab for that shell session. Multiple sessions can be open simultaneously as tabs in the drawer. The terminal is rendered with xterm.js and connected bidirectionally to the pod via `kubectl exec` using `@kubernetes/client-node`'s `Exec` class over a WebSocket-based stream. Each tab shows the pod name and container name as its label. Closing a tab terminates the underlying shell process.
acceptance_criteria: Pod detail panel shows a 'Shell' button (only visible when a pod is selected)
Clicking 'Shell' opens the bottom drawer (if not already open) and adds a new terminal tab labeled '<podName> / <containerName>'
If the pod has multiple containers, a dropdown in the detail panel (or in the tab header) lets the user pick which container to exec into; defaults to first container
Bottom drawer is resizable (drag handle at the top edge); minimum height 150px, default height 300px
Each tab renders an xterm.js Terminal with the fit addon; the terminal fills the tab panel width and resizes on drawer resize
IPC handler `k8s:pod:exec` is registered in the main process using `@kubernetes/client-node` `Exec.exec()` with a WebSocket stream; stdin, stdout, stderr are piped bidirectionally
Terminal input (keystrokes) is sent from renderer to main via `ipcRenderer.send('k8s:pod:exec:input', { sessionId, data })`; main writes to the exec stdin stream
Terminal output (stdout + stderr) arrives from main via `ipcRenderer.on('k8s:pod:exec:output', ({ sessionId, data }) => ...)` and is written to the xterm Terminal instance
Closing a tab sends `ipcRenderer.send('k8s:pod:exec:close', { sessionId })` and main terminates the stream; the tab is removed from the drawer
When all tabs are closed the bottom drawer hides itself
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Install `@xterm/xterm` and `@xterm/addon-fit`. Use `Exec` from `@kubernetes/client-node`; call `exec(namespace, podName, containerName, command, stdout, stderr, stdin, tty, statusCallback)` with `command = ['/bin/sh']` (fall back to `/bin/bash` on error). Use a UUID (`crypto.randomUUID()`) as `sessionId` to correlate IPC messages. Store active sessions in a `Map<sessionId, { stream, webSocket }>` in main process module scope. The bottom drawer and tab strip are new renderer components: `BottomDrawer` (position fixed at bottom, z-index above content) and `ShellTabs` (tab list + panels). Use a Zustand slice or local state to hold `shellSessions: Array<{ sessionId, podName, containerName }>`. Terminal resize: call `fitAddon.fit()` inside a `ResizeObserver` on the drawer panel div.

stories.title: Multi-cluster tree view

The namespace filter continues to work within the active context.
acceptance_criteria: Tree view lists every context from kubeconfig as a top-level collapsible node (node label = context name)
Each context node contains the same sub-tree structure as the current single-cluster tree (Cluster, Workloads, Networking, Config, Events groups with their leaf items)
Clicking a resource leaf under a context sets `selectedContext: string` and `selectedResourceType: string` in the Zustand app store; the leaf is highlighted

Main process maintains a per-context API client cache: `Map<contextName, { coreV1: CoreV1Api, appsV1: AppsV1Api }>`. On first use of a context a new KubeConfig is created with `kc.loadFromDefault(); kc.setCurrentContext(contextName)` and its API clients are stored

All existing resource-fetch IPC handlers (k8s:namespaces:list, k8s:nodes:list, k8s:pods:list, k8s:deployments:list, k8s:replicasets:list, k8s:statefulsets:list, k8s:daemonsets:list, k8s:services:list, k8s:ingresses:list, k8s:configmaps:list, k8s:secrets:list, k8s:events:list) accept an optional `contextName` parameter and route to the correct per-context client; if omitted they fall back to the current default context
All renderer resource-view components pass `selectedContext` from the Zustand store when invoking `window.api.*` IPC calls
AppBar context badge shows the value of `selectedContext` (or the kubeconfig current-context if nothing is selected yet)
Cluster-type badge (EKS / AKS / Local) is derived per-context from the context's cluster server URL and shown next to each context node label in the tree
The namespace filter (`selectedNamespace` in Zustand store) resets to `null` whenever `selectedContext` changes
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Per-context client cache lives in main process module scope (e.g. `const clientCache = new Map()`). Use `kc.makeApiClient(CoreV1Api)` after setting the context. Do not invalidate the cache on each call — reuse existing clients for the same context. Pass `contextName` as the first property of the args object for each IPC handler, e.g. `ipcMain.handle('k8s:pods:list', async (_e, { contextName, namespace }) => {...})`. Renderer calls become e.g. `window.api.listPods({ contextName: selectedContext, namespace: selectedNamespace })`. Update preload contextBridge accordingly. The existing `k8s:contexts:list` handler (S02) already returns all context names — use it to populate the tree on mount.

stories.title: EKS credential check
stories.description: Before connecting to an EKS cluster, verify that valid AWS credentials exist in the environment. The app must detect either static credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) or temporary credentials (AWS_SESSION_TOKEN alongside the static keys, or credentials loaded from ~/.aws/credentials / instance metadata). If no usable credentials are found, show a clear error message rather than silently failing on the first k8s API call.
acceptance_criteria: On app startup, an IPC handler `aws:credentials:check` is registered in the main process

The handler checks, in order: environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY), ~/.aws/credentials file (default profile or AWS_PROFILE), and instance/container metadata (IMDSv2 / ECS task role)
Handler returns `{ valid: true, type: 'env' | 'file' | 'metadata' | 'none' }` — never throws
If `valid` is false, the renderer shows a non-dismissible warning banner: 'No AWS credentials found. EKS clusters may not be accessible.'
If `valid` is true and `type` is `'env'` with AWS_SESSION_TOKEN set, the banner shows an info notice: 'Using temporary AWS credentials.'
If `valid` is true with static or file/metadata credentials, no banner is shown
Credential check runs once at startup; a 'Re-check' button in the banner triggers it again
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Do NOT use the AWS SDK — read credentials purely from env vars and ~/.aws/credentials (INI parse). For metadata, attempt a HEAD to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ with a 1-second timeout; if it responds, treat as valid metadata credentials. Renderer should call this handler on mount via useEffect.

stories.title: Edit RBAC resources in BottomDrawer
stories.description: Replace the modal-based edit UX for Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding, and ServiceAccount with a BottomDrawer tab. Clicking 'Edit' on a resource detail panel opens a new drawer tab containing a YAML editor panel. stories.title: Node resource usage metrics in Node detail panel
stories.description: The Node list and detail panel currently show conditions and status but no CPU or memory usage. Add live CPU and memory usage metrics to each Node's detail panel using the Kubernetes Metrics API (metrics.k8s.io), the same source used for pod metrics in S46-S47.
acceptance_criteria: New IPC handler k8s:node:metrics fetches node metrics from the Metrics API using CustomObjectsApi getClusterCustomObject for group 'metrics.k8s.io', version 'v1beta1', plural 'nodes'; returns array of { nodeName, cpuUsage (nanocores as string), memoryUsage (bytes as string) }
Node detail panel gains a 'Resource Usage' section showing CPU and memory as progress bars: usage / allocatable capacity expressed as percentage
Allocatable CPU and memory come from node.status.allocatable already available in the k8s:nodes:list response; add these fields to the serialized node object if not already present
If Metrics API is unavailable (404 or 403), show a muted 'Metrics unavailable' message in the section instead of an error
Node list table gains two new columns: CPU% and Mem% showing the same percentage values (fetched once on load alongside the node list)
Metrics refresh on the same interval as the node list auto-refresh
window.api exposes getNodeMetrics via preload contextBridge
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Metrics API must be installed in the cluster (metrics-server). Handle gracefully when absent. CPU nanocores: divide by 1e9 for cores. Memory bytes: display in Mi or Gi. Allocatable values from node.status.allocatable are strings like '4' (CPU cores) or '8Gi' (memory) — parse them to compute percentage.

stories.title: Log search and filter in pod log panel
stories.description: The PodLogPanel tails logs but provides no way to search or filter lines. Add a search input that filters displayed log lines client-side by substring or regex. Matching text is highlighted within each line. A match count indicator shows how many lines match.
acceptance_criteria: PodLogPanel gains a search input above the log output area; placeholder text 'Filter logs…'
Typing in the search input filters the displayed lines to only those containing the search string (case-insensitive substring match by default)
A toggle button next to the input switches between substring and regex mode; in regex mode, invalid regex shows a red border on the input but does not crash
Matching text within each displayed line is wrapped in a <mark> or highlighted <span> with a distinct background color
A match count badge shows 'N lines match' updated as the user types
When search is active, auto-scroll to bottom is paused; clearing the search input resumes auto-scroll
The search input and mode toggle are preserved when the tab is re-activated (state lives in the tab component, not the store)
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: All filtering is client-side — the log buffer is already in component state. Do not re-fetch or re-start the log stream when filtering. Keep the full unfiltered log buffer in state; derive the displayed lines from it using useMemo with the search term as dependency. For regex mode, wrap the match attempt in try/catch.

stories.title: Pod and Service port-forward to localhost
stories.description: Add a 'Port Forward' button to Pod and Service detail panels. Clicking it opens a BottomDrawer tab with a form to specify local port and target port. The main process creates a TCP server on the local port and proxies data to/from the pod port using the Kubernetes port-forward protocol over the API server WebSocket.
acceptance_criteria: Pod detail panel gains a 'Port Forward' button in the header action area
Service detail panel gains a 'Port Forward' button in the header action area

Clicking 'Port Forward' opens a BottomDrawer tab of type 'port-forward' with fields: tabKey ('port-forward:<kind>:<namespace>/<name>'), resourceKind ('Pod'|'Service'), resourceName, namespace, localPort (number), targetPort (number)
DrawerTab and DrawerTabInput unions gain a 'port-forward' variant

The tab renders a PortForwardPanel with: local port input (default 8080), target port input (pre-filled from first pod/service port), Start/Stop button, status line showing 'Forwarding localhost:<localPort> → <resourceName>:<targetPort>' or error message

New IPC handler 'portforward:start' accepts { resourceKind, namespace, name, localPort, targetPort, sessionId }; for Pod kind uses the k8s port-forward API (POST to /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/portforward with SPDY upgrade); for Service kind resolves to a backing pod first then forwards; returns { success: boolean, error?: string }
New IPC handler 'portforward:stop' accepts { sessionId }; closes the TCP server and WebSocket
On successful start, status shows the forwarding address; on error, shows error inline in panel
window.api exposes startPortForward and stopPortForward via preload contextBridge
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Port-forwarding via k8s API requires SPDY or WebSocket upgrade — use the @kubernetes/client-node PortForward helper class (it handles the SPDY framing). Import it from '@kubernetes/client-node'. For Services, list endpoints to find a ready pod IP, then forward to that pod. Local TCP server: use Node.js net.createServer. One session per tab; stop on tab close.

stories.title: ResourceQuota and LimitRange view with usage visualization
stories.description: Add ResourceQuota and LimitRange to the tree under a new 'Governance' group. ResourceQuota detail shows a usage bar for each resource (used vs hard limit), making it immediately obvious when a namespace is near its limits.
acceptance_criteria: TreeView gains a 'Governance' group with items: 'ResourceQuotas' and 'LimitRanges'

New IPC handler k8s:resourcequotas:list uses CoreV1Api listResourceQuotaForAllNamespaces; returns: name, namespace, hard (map of resource→limit string), used (map of resource→used string), creationTimestamp
New IPC handler k8s:limitranges:list uses CoreV1Api listLimitRangeForAllNamespaces; returns: name, namespace, limits (array of {type, max, min, default, defaultRequest}), creationTimestamp
ResourceQuotasView list columns: Name, Namespace, Resources (count of tracked resources), Age

ResourceQuota detail panel shows each tracked resource as a row: resource name, used value, hard limit, and a progress bar (used/hard as percentage); rows where used > 80% of hard are highlighted in yellow, rows where used >= hard in red
LimitRangesView list columns: Name, Namespace, Types (Container/Pod/PersistentVolumeClaim), Age
LimitRange detail panel shows each limit type with max, min, default, defaultRequest values in a table
Namespace filter applies to both views
window.api exposes listResourceQuotas and listLimitRanges via preload contextBridge
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: ResourceQuota used/hard values are strings like '500m', '1Gi', '10'. Parse them for the progress bar percentage: for CPU use parseCpuString, for memory use parseMemoryString, for counts use parseInt. A simple parseResourceValue(value: string): number utility in utils.ts handles the conversion.

stories.title: Global resource search across all resource types
stories.description: Add a global search bar in the AppBar that lets users find any resource by name across all resource types and namespaces. Results appear in a dropdown list grouped by resource type. Clicking a result navigates to that resource type and selects the item.
acceptance_criteria: AppBar gains a search input (Command+K or Ctrl+K keyboard shortcut focuses it)
Typing at least 2 characters triggers a search: calls all existing list IPC handlers in parallel and filters results client-side by name substring (case-insensitive)
Results shown in a dropdown popover grouped by resource type (Pods, Deployments, Services, etc.); up to 5 results per group
Each result shows: resource name, namespace (if applicable), resource kind icon or label
Clicking a result sets selectedResourceType to the resource's type and selectedItem to the matching resource object, then closes the dropdown
Pressing Escape or clicking outside closes the dropdown without navigating
A loading indicator shows while IPC calls are in flight; if all return empty, shows 'No results found'
Search state (query, open/closed) is local component state — not persisted to the store
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: No new IPC handlers — reuse all existing list handlers. Debounce the search trigger by 300ms to avoid firing on every keystroke. The search fetches with the currently selected context. Resource kind grouping order: Pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, ReplicaSets, Services, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Namespaces, Nodes, ServiceAccounts, Roles, ClusterRoles, RoleBindings, ClusterRoleBindings. Use a shadcn Popover or Command component for the dropdown.

stories.title: YAML diff view before applying edits
stories.description: When editing a resource in the yaml-edit BottomDrawer tab, show a diff between the original YAML (as loaded) and the current textarea content before the user clicks Save. This prevents accidental overwrites and makes it clear what will change.
acceptance_criteria: YamlEditPanel gains a 'Show diff' toggle button next to the Save button

When toggled on, the textarea is replaced by a side-by-side or unified diff view showing removed lines (red background) and added lines (green background) between initialYaml and the current textarea content
When toggled off, the textarea is shown again with the user's current edits preserved
The diff is computed client-side using the 'diff' npm package (diff.createPatch or diff.diffLines); no IPC call needed
If the textarea content is identical to initialYaml, the diff view shows 'No changes' and the Save button is disabled
The diff view is read-only; the user must toggle back to textarea to make further edits
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Install the 'diff' npm package (MIT license, no native deps). Use diff.diffLines(initialYaml, currentYaml) to get an array of change objects. Render each line with appropriate background color using Tailwind. The diff view does not need to be a full Monaco diff editor — a simple line-by-line render is sufficient.

stories.title: Deployment rollout history and rollback
stories.description: Add rollout history and rollback capability to the Deployment detail panel. Users can see previous ReplicaSet revisions, view the pod template diff between revisions, and roll back to a specific revision.
acceptance_criteria: Deployment detail panel gains a 'Rollout History' section showing past revisions as a table: revision number, change-cause annotation, image(s), created date

New IPC handler k8s:deployment:history fetches ReplicaSets owned by the deployment (using AppsV1Api listNamespacedReplicaSet with labelSelector matching the deployment's selector), extracts the 'deployment.kubernetes.io/revision' annotation, and returns them sorted by revision descending
Each row in the history table has a 'Rollback to this revision' button

New IPC handler k8s:deployment:rollback accepts { namespace, name, revision } and patches the deployment with the rollback annotation (sets spec.rollbackTo.revision or patches the pod template from the target ReplicaSet)
Clicking rollback shows an AlertDialog confirmation, then calls the IPC handler, shows a success toast, and refreshes the deployment detail
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Rollback implementation: fetch the target ReplicaSet's pod template spec (from the RS with the matching revision annotation), then patch the Deployment's spec.template with that spec using AppsV1Api patchNamespacedDeployment. This is equivalent to kubectl rollout undo --to-revision=N. The change-cause annotation key is 'kubernetes.io/change-cause'.

stories.title: NetworkPolicy list view and detail view
stories.description: Add NetworkPolicy to the tree under the Networking group. The list shows which namespaces have policies and the pod selector. The detail panel shows ingress and egress rules in a readable format.
acceptance_criteria: TreeView Networking group gains a 'NetworkPolicies' item

New IPC handler k8s:networkpolicies:list uses NetworkingV1Api listNetworkPolicyForAllNamespaces; returns: name, namespace, podSelector (as label string), policyTypes (Ingress/Egress), ingressRuleCount, egressRuleCount, creationTimestamp
NetworkPoliciesView list columns: Name, Namespace, Pod Selector, Policy Types, Ingress Rules, Egress Rules, Age
Detail panel shows: podSelector labels, policyTypes, each ingress rule (from CIDRs/namespaceSelectors/podSelectors + ports), each egress rule in the same format
Namespace filter and name filter apply
window.api exposes listNetworkPolicies via preload contextBridge
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: NetworkingV1Api is already imported in k8s-handlers.ts for Ingress. Reuse it. Pod selector with empty matchLabels means 'all pods in namespace' — display as 'All pods'. Rules with empty from/to array mean 'deny all'. Serialize ingress/egress rules as plain objects; render them as collapsible rows in the detail panel.

stories.title: PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) list view and detail view
stories.description: Add PodDisruptionBudget to the tree under Governance. PDBs are critical during node drains and rollouts. The list shows current disruption allowance (how many pods can be disrupted right now).
acceptance_criteria: TreeView Governance group (from S75) gains a 'PodDisruptionBudgets' item

New IPC handler k8s:pdbs:list uses PolicyV1Api listPodDisruptionBudgetForAllNamespaces; returns: name, namespace, minAvailable, maxUnavailable, currentHealthy, desiredHealthy, disruptionsAllowed, creationTimestamp
PDBsView list columns: Name, Namespace, Min Available, Max Unavailable, Current Healthy, Disruptions Allowed, Age
Disruptions Allowed cell colored red when value is 0 (no disruptions allowed)
Detail panel shows: selector, minAvailable, maxUnavailable, currentHealthy, desiredHealthy, disruptionsAllowed, expectedPods, labels, annotations
Namespace filter and name filter apply
window.api exposes listPDBs via preload contextBridge
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Use PolicyV1Api (policy/v1), available in k8s 1.21+. If cluster uses older policy/v1beta1, handle the 404 gracefully with a 'PDB API not available on this cluster' message. disruptionsAllowed=0 means a node drain would block — highlight clearly.

stories.title: Endpoints and EndpointSlices view
stories.description: Add Endpoints to the Networking group. Endpoints show which pod IPs back a Service, which is essential for debugging 503s and service routing issues. The detail panel shows ready vs not-ready addresses and their target pod names.
acceptance_criteria: TreeView Networking group gains an 'Endpoints' item
New IPC handler k8s:endpoints:list uses CoreV1Api listEndpointsForAllNamespaces; returns: name, namespace, readyAddressCount, notReadyAddressCount, ports, creationTimestamp
EndpointsView list columns: Name, Namespace, Ready, Not Ready, Ports, Age
Detail panel shows: for each subset — ready addresses (IP + target pod name/namespace), not-ready addresses, ports
Not-ready addresses highlighted in yellow/amber
Namespace filter and name filter apply
window.api exposes listEndpoints via preload contextBridge
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Endpoints name matches Service name in same namespace — this is a k8s convention. The detail panel implicitly shows which Service these endpoints back. notReadyAddresses exist in the subset when pods fail readiness probes. Do not add EndpointSlices in this story to keep scope small.

stories.title: Multi-container log merge in pod log panel
stories.description: The current PodLogPanel shows one container's log at a time. Add a 'Merge all containers' mode that interleaves log lines from all containers in the pod, prefixed with the container name, in a single scrolling view. Useful for debugging init containers and sidecars.
acceptance_criteria: PodLogPanel gains a 'Merge containers' toggle button in the header (only shown when the pod has more than one container)
When merge mode is active, the panel starts log streams for all containers simultaneously and interleaves their lines in arrival order
Each line is prefixed with '[container-name] ' in a muted color to distinguish sources
Each container stream uses a separate sessionId (e.g. 'pod-log-<podName>-<containerName>-<ts>'); all are tracked in component state and stopped on unmount or toggle-off
The container selector dropdown is hidden when merge mode is active
The search/filter from S73 applies to the merged output
Switching merge mode off returns to single-container mode showing the previously selected container
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Each container's stream calls the existing k8s:pod:log:start IPC handler with its own sessionId. The merged buffer is a useState array of { containerName, line } objects; display is derived via useMemo. Order of lines is insertion order (arrival from IPC events), not timestamp-sorted — timestamp sorting would require parsing log lines which is format-dependent.

stories.title: kubectl-style resource copy to clipboard
stories.description: Add a copy-to-clipboard menu to resource detail panels. Users frequently need to copy a pod name, namespace, or full kubectl command to paste into a terminal. A small copy button or dropdown in the detail panel header provides one-click access.
acceptance_criteria: Resource detail panels (Pods, Deployments, Services, and all other resource types with detail panels) gain a copy dropdown button in the header action area (copy icon, ghost variant)
The dropdown menu has three options: 'Copy name', 'Copy namespace/name', 'Copy kubectl command'
'Copy name' copies the resource name to the clipboard (e.g. 'nginx-abc123')
'Copy namespace/name' copies '<namespace>/<name>' (e.g. 'production/nginx-abc123'); for cluster-scoped resources copies only the name
'Copy kubectl command' copies a full kubectl get command (e.g. 'kubectl get pod nginx-abc123 -n production -o yaml') using the correct resource kind singular (pod, deployment, service, etc.)
After clicking any option, a brief 'Copied!' toast appears
Clipboard write uses navigator.clipboard.writeText (renderer process has clipboard access in Electron)
No TypeScript compile errors
stories.notes: Resource kind to kubectl noun mapping: Pod→pod, Deployment→deployment, StatefulSet→statefulset, DaemonSet→daemonset, ReplicaSet→replicaset, Service→service, Ingress→ingress, ConfigMap→configmap, Secret→secret, Namespace→namespace, Node→node, ServiceAccount→serviceaccount, Role→role, ClusterRole→clusterrole, RoleBinding→rolebinding, ClusterRoleBinding→clusterrolebinding. Use a shadcn DropdownMenu component. No IPC needed — clipboard.writeText runs in renderer.
